deep_reading.architecture_zh: 原始架构是 table-wise sharding：每个 embedding 表放在单一 GPU 上，所有 GPU 参与跨节点 all-to-all。最终架构采用 2D Parallel：GPU 按节点分组，组内像原来一样切分表，组间持有完整模型副本；All-to-All 只走节点内 NVLink，跨节点仅用 AllReduce 做副本同步。通信层用 FBGEMM QComms 将 embedding 张量从 FP32 压缩为 FP8 作为线格式；用均衡分片（hash partition 数对齐 GPU 数）和带宽感知 reshape（embedding 维减半、行数翻倍）降低负载；checkpoint 从 TorchSnapshot 迁移到 PyTorch Distributed Checkpoint，支持不同 world size 的 load-time resharding。
business_implications_zh: 多节点训练解锁了单节点不可能训练的更大、更深、更宽的模型，是后续 teacher-student distillation 等策略的前提。
更大模型在 Homefeed 和 Related Pins 等最高流量推荐面上带来统计显著的 engagement 提升。
训练加速缩短实验周期：原来需要数周的验证现在只需一小部分时间，加快迭代。
优化前 3 倍 GPU/成本只换来 21% 吞吐；优化后 4 节点 3.9x、8 节点 7.5x，接近线性的扩展把更多算力转化为实际吞吐，改善单位成本效率。
该框架已扩展到 Homefeed、Related Pins、ads 和多节点 distillation 工作流，愿景是用 scalability 作为更强大模型、更低成本的杠杆。

evidence_refs.heading: From One Project to a Playbook

deep_reading.implementation_zh: 优化分五步叠加：(1) QComms：量化 embedding 通信载荷，2 节点 scaling 1.13x→1.57x，4 节点 1.21x→2.3x，最大 SendRecv 降低 75% 以上，且训练 loss 收敛等价。(2) Balanced sharding：hash partition 数匹配 GPU 数，2 节点 +5.3%，4 节点 +15.2%；仅在 benchmark 验证，生产 serving 侧 embedding 配置限制独立采用。(3) Bandwidth-aware embedding optimization：embedding 维度减半、行数翻倍，保持容量不变，2 节点 1.78x，4 节点 2.8x。(4) 2D Parallel（AllReduce 优化版）：按节点分组、组间复制完整模型，通信重叠使 wall time 从 25.68ms 降到 16.98ms，2 节点 1.90x，4 节点 3.6x。(5) 2D Parallel（All-to-All 优化版）：翻转拓扑，All-to-All 留在节点内，跨节点 AllReduce，All-to-All 延迟 78ms→13ms，2 节点 2.0x，4 节点 3.9x。最终扩展到 8 节点（64 GPU）7.5x、490k examples/sec；另外 torch.compile 给单节点 forward/loss 带来 55% 吞吐提升。
lessons_zh: You can't optimize what you don't measure：并排比较单节点/双节点 profile 直接定位到分布式 embedding 通信。
Optimizations compound：QComms 单独只到 1.57x（2 节点），达到 3.9x/7.5x 需要同时处理 payload 体积、payload 形状和并行拓扑。
Communication dominates at scale：对 embedding-heavy 推荐模型，纯计算优化无法解决多节点扩展，必须直接处理通信层。
可复用 playbook：先 profile 瓶颈，再减少线上字节、按带宽 reshape payload、把昂贵通信留在本地拓扑中；已系统应用到 foundation model 家族。
生产分布式训练中的大版本框架升级本身就是一个项目；PyTorch/TorchRec 升级中多个问题只在多节点运行时暴露。
limitations_zh: 所有数据来自 Pinterest 自己的 p4d/A100 环境；硬件无关性是设计主张，文中没有在更新硬件上的实测。
Balanced sharding 优化只在 benchmark 验证，未在生产独立采用，因为 serving 侧 embedding 配置约束。
文章聚焦 scalability，不覆盖 training efficiency 的全面优化。
Scaling factor 都以优化后的单节点为基线；8 节点结果只在完整五层优化栈下给出，未提供 8 节点上各技术的单独消融。
结论针对 embedding-heavy 推荐模型（99% 参数在 embedding），不一定直接迁移到 dense/transformer-heavy 模型。
框架升级问题（Triton/NCCL/profiler）只在多节点运行中暴露，意味着单节点验证不足以发现生产问题。
production_constraints_zh: 没有 AWS EFA 时，加第二个 8-GPU 节点反而让训练比单节点慢 5 倍；EFA 的 OS-bypass 网络是可用性的前提。
即使有 EFA，未优化时 3 个额外节点/3 倍 GPU/3 倍成本只换来 21% 更多吞吐。
多节点训练需要框架级投资：从 TorchSnapshot 迁移到 DCP，PyTorch 2.1→2.5→2.6、TorchRec 1.1 升级，过程中要处理 Triton 版本不匹配、NCCL build 冲突和 memory profiler 崩溃。
Balanced sharding 在 benchmark 有效，但生产 serving 侧 embedding 配置约束使其无法独立上线。
embedding 表超过单 GPU 显存，必须分片；forward 的 all-to-all 通信量与 batch size 和 embedding 维度成比例。
results_zh: 2 节点 scaling 从 1.13x 提升到 2.0x；4 节点从 1.21x 提升到 3.9x（理论理想值的 97.5%）。
扩展到 8 节点（64 GPU）得到 7.5x scaling（93.75% 理想值），吞吐 490k examples/sec。
从 pre-EFA 基线到完全优化，2 节点多节点吞吐端到端提升 13x；4 节点相对 EFA 基线提升 5.3x。
All-to-All 延迟从 78ms 降到 13ms（约 6x 降低/83% 减少）。
QComms 使 NCCL 通信量减少 75%，最大的 NCCL SendRecv 操作下降超过 75%。
诊断时两节点 forward 从单节点 410ms 增至 710ms，GPU util 97.7% 但 SM efficiency 54.54%，瓶颈是分布式 embedding collective。
更大模型启用 teacher-student distillation，并在 Homefeed/Related Pins 产生统计显著的 engagement 提升，实验周期从数周缩短到一小部分时间。
torch.compile 给单节点 forward/loss 带来 55% 吞吐提升。
deep_reading.system_context_zh: Pinterest 的 foundation model 为超过 6 亿月活跃用户提供推荐，预训练数据覆盖两年用户行为，并部署在 Home feed 与 Related Pins 两个最重要的推荐系统中。模型是 embedding-heavy：约 99% 参数在 embedding 表，dense transformer 只占剩余部分；embedding 表超出单 GPU 显存，因此用 TorchRec DistributedModelParallel 在 GPU 间分片，forward 时通过 NCCL all-to-all 交换 embedding lookup。测量环境为 AWS p4d（A100 GPU），并启用 EFA OS-bypass 网络。
tradeoffs_zh: QComms 把线格式从 FP32 压到 FP8，与计算精度解耦；收益是通信量下降，代价是需要验证模型质量不受影响（文中验证 loss 收敛等价）。
Balanced sharding 改善负载均衡，但更多设备时收益更大；在 Pinterest 生产环境受 serving 侧 embedding 配置约束，只能作为 benchmark 验证。
Bandwidth-aware reshape 用 embedding 维减半、行数翻倍保持容量不变，体现“瓶颈是带宽而非参数容量”的判断。
2D Parallel 把昂贵的 All-to-All 限制在节点内，跨节点用 AllReduce；这是用组内完整副本/同步换取跨节点通信量下降的拓扑取舍。
torch.compile 的 55% 单节点提升是独立优化，与多节点扩展栈互补，不解决通信瓶颈。
框架升级本身耗时且容易出错，但落后于上游的代价会累积。

excerpt: Sheng Huang | Software Engineer, AI Platform; Pong Eksombatchai | Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Sciences; Saurabh Vishwas Joshi | Software Engineer, AI Platform; Gaurav Arora | Software Engineer, AI Platform; Karthik Anantha Padmanabhan | Engineering Director, AI Platform At Pinterest, foundation models power recommendations for over 600 million monthly active users. Our latest Foundation Model (ACM RecSys 2025) pre-trains on two years of user activity data and is deployed into Home feed and Related Pins ranking, the platform’s two most important recommendation systems. Multi-node distributed training is the key to unlocking the next level of that capacity. ¹ But when we first attempted multi-node training, adding a second machine made training 5x slower, producing a scaling factor of roughly 0.2x. Enabling AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for OS-bypass networking fixed the networking layer and recovered a viable baseline, but scaling was still poor: 1.13x at 2 nodes and 1.21x at 4 nodes. Three extra nodes, 3x more GPUs, 3x more cost, yet only 21% more throughput. This post describes how we took 2-node scaling from 1.13x to 2.0x and 4-node scaling from 1.21x to 3.9x (97.5% of ideal), then extended to 8 nodes at 7.5x. The larger models this unlocked have driven significant engagement gains across Pinterest’s recommendation surfaces. Figure 1: Training scalability before and after optimization. Left: before EFA and optimization, adding a second node degraded throughput to 0.2x of single-node. Right: after optimization, scaling is near-linear across 2, 4, and 8 nodes, with 8-node reaching 7.5x (93.75% of ideal). Background Training scalability measures whether adding more resources yields proportionally more throughput. Training efficiency measures how much throughput you extract from the same resources. This post focuses on scalability. Our Foundation Ranking Model is embedding-heavy: approximately 99% of parameters reside in embedding tables, with the dense transformer layers accounting for the remainder. These tables exceed single-GPU memory, so we shard them across GPUs using TorchRec’s DistributedModelParallel. Each GPU holds a subset of tables, and during the forward pass, GPUs exchange embedding lookups via NCCL all-to-all operations. This solves the memory problem but creates a new one: every forward pass generates All-to-All communication proportional to batch size and embedding dimension, and at multi-node scale, that communication cost dominates everything else. Where We Started Multi-node training at Pinterest was initially unusable. Without AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), which provides OS-bypass networking for NCCL, adding a second 8-GPU node didn’t just fail to help. It made training 5x slower, a scaling factor of roughly 0.2x, pushing performance well below the single-node baseline. Enabling EFA changed the picture. By bypassing the OS network stack for cross-node GPU communication, EFA delivered a 5x throughput improvement and made distributed training viable for the first time. But viable is not the same as efficient. Even with EFA in place, scaling remained poor: Three extra nodes, 3x more GPUs, 3x more cost, yet only 21% more throughput. These numbers became our starting point. Everything that follows in this post builds from here. Figure 2: Baseline scaling factor vs. nodes. The blue line shows observed scaling with EFA enabled: 1.13x at 2 nodes and 1.21x at 4 nodes, nearly flat against the theoretical ideal (dashed). The red zone indicates degraded performance below single-node, where our pre-EFA results fell. Diagnosis We instrumented training with PyTorch Profiler and collected NCCL traces on single-node and two-node configurations. Rather than guessing, we let the data tell us where the problem was. The two-node trace told the story immediately. The forward pass, which took ~410ms on a single node, ballooned to ~710ms on two nodes. summary_zh: Pinterest 分享了推荐基础模型在多节点训练上的近线性扩展经验：通过启用 EFA 并优化 NCCL 通信，将 2 节点扩展系数从 1.13x 提升到 2.0x，4 节点到 3.9x，8 节点达到 7.5x，从而支撑更大规模推荐模型与业务增长。
title: Achieving Near-Linear Training Scalability for Pinterest’s Foundation Models
